740110101.text: Hey, what are you doing under a waterfall? Are you gonna take a bath or something?

740110102.text: Um, if that's the case, we won't disturb you...

740110103.text: What bath? I am pondering some profound questions. If I must say... I suppose I am "meditating."

740110104.text: If you hadn't come thundering along and interrupted my train of thought, perhaps I would have already come up with the answers.

740110106.text: I read in a book that if you run into something you can't make sense of, if you just "meditate," maybe you'll find the answers. I didn't misunderstand that, right?

740110108.text: Let's see... A human most strange and a rainbow balloon. You two must be from outside the village?

740110109.text: #Right! Paimon's Paimon, and {M#he}{F#she}'s {NICKNAME}... Wait a sec. Though you're right to say that we're not from here, what do you mean, a rainbow balloon?

740110110.text: Oh, right. You might not see it that way... I almost forgot about that again...

740110111.text: #Let me think... Right. {NICKNAME}, what does Paimon look like to you?

subQuests.subQuestName: Go to the place where the book is hidden

740110201.text: Aaand we're here! If we dive down below this "entrance," we'll find the place where that scholar once hid the books.

740110202.text: Huh... But it looks like an ordinary pond. What sort of entrance are you talking about?

740110203.text: Ah, right, it is being hidden, after all, so you won't be able to see... Hehe, just watch, then.

740110204.text: Canotila takes out something that looks like a key, tracing the air along some unseen trail.\nThere is a soft chime, and the shallow pool before you suddenly becomes unfathomably deep.

740110206.text: Wow, Paimon couldn't tell how you did that!

740110207.text: Well, I can't quite explain it either... But while others can't see it, there are actually all sorts of fissures here.

740110208.text: As long as I use my token to draw a line across those fissures, I can do some incredible things.

740110209.text: That said, I don't know why they are only present here. As such, I did a lot of research... until I found that indecipherable book...

740110210.text: It has much to do with me and my token, and I'm also certain that if I figure it out, I'll know why I'm special in this way.

740110213.text: Well, then! That's enough of that! Let's go inside!

740110214.text: I must find a way to understand that strange book.

740112501.text: Awesome! Let's put another page in now, shall we?

subQuests.subQuestName: Go to the place where the book is hidden

740110701.text: Even when "meditating," I can't make heads or tails of what comes before and after.

740110702.text: As such, though I can understand just a little bit, I still don't know what it is really saying... If I'm not mistaken, however, the book is still missing a lot of content.

740110703.text: The notebook does mention a few locations.

740110704.text: Oh! So you mean that these locations might be clues?

740110705.text: Locations? Yes, the names of locations are written between important sections. Could it be trying to tell us where critical parts of the text are hidden?

740110706.text: I mean, I've guessed as much in the past, but I've never left Elynas, so...

740110707.text: In that case, why don't you stay here, Canotila? We'll go investigate the places in the notebook. Maybe we'll find the missing pieces!

740110708.text: And besides, it's related to Elynas, so there's no way we're going to ignore it!

740110709.text: Alright! In that case, I'm counting on you two.

740110710.text: If you find anything, just bring it back. I'll be waiting here for you.

740110401.text: If we can find the missing parts of this book and put them back where they belong, maybe we'll be able to understand more...

740110501.text: And then we just need to concentrate and "meditate" on the book, like before.

740110503.text: The edges of the page gradually blur. After a spell of dizziness, the words seem to become clearer...

740110504.text: Wow! This time, even Paimon could start to understand! Seems like the confusion was all due to the pages that were missing before, huh?

740110601.text: Hmm, based on my previous results, that scholar must have been conducting research on Elynas or something.

740110602.text: Uh... Then this book must record things that happened a long time ago!

740110603.text: Yes. But I still can't understand exactly what happened.

740111221.text: As you start meditating again, you once more attempt to understand the page's contents.\nThe edges of the page blur, and the incomprehensible shapes that line it leap forth, as if mounted on a pop-up book.\nYet, before you can make sense of what is happening, there is a rush of noise all around you, and you return to the world as it was.

740111222.text: Well, Paimon can read the words now, but the author's intended meaning is still a total mystery!

740111223.text: We'll just have to put this last page in and see what we get. Maybe the contents will link up, or something!

740111201.text: As you read faster and faster, you fall into a trance and arrive again in that mysterious space.\nThe same voice from before rings out.

740111202.text: "...No matter how many times I run the calculations, the results are the same. After a few hundred years, all the birthing waters of the world will dry up, and a few hundred years after that, the world will become as it appears now before us. This is quite the predicament."\n"...Hey, come on now, don't cry! There's nothing to be afraid of. I'm here, aren't I? Don't you trust me? Also, Alain and the others will definitely help. Also, I bet you'll definitely be able to survive in this world. You're special..."\n"...I know, I know. You're worried that constitution of others is different from yours. That's reasonable. Well, that's why we need to continue researching the things left behind by the Golden Troupe. Perhaps we'll discover some new possibilities. We'll go back to the Narzissenkreuz Institute together and take a look, okay?"

740111203.text: The voice drifts away again. After what feels like a long time — though, in this world, time seems to no longer measure changes in matter — you hear the voice once more.

740111204.text: "It looks like he won't help us anymore. You're the only one I can rely on now. Hey, come on! Don't be like that. I'm sad too, but I won't cry until after the fat lady sings. Moreover, we still have to find a way to cure him."\n"...Don't be scared, it'll all go smoothly. There are already lots of people willing to listen to us. If we want to persuade them further... Besides belief, we'll also need ceremony..."\n"...As for the name, we'll call it the 'Book of Revealing,' and put it in the form of a book. We'll use our secret cipher to write it. Everyone only sees the world that their cognitive framework allows them to see. But using this method, we can share the visions we have foreseen with others..."

740111205.text: Just as you begin to listen closely to what the voice is saying, it begins to gradually fade away...\nAt the same time, you feel the world around you suddenly begin to collapse, and with a roaring sound resounding, you wake again.

740111206.text: Was that an earthquake just now?

740111207.text: Earthquake? What earthquake? Nothing happened here...

740111208.text: Paimon did get a little dizzy, but you looked like you'd fainted! You didn't wind up in some mysterious space again, did you?

740111209.text: Just what's going on with that weird space, anyhow... And if you think about it, it's pretty dangerous too! What if you go in and can't get back out?

740111210.text: So just what did you encounter inside?

740111212.text: Huh? The pages we found before did mention something about deductions and calculations, too... Could it be that the things revealed inside that space were actually the result of such deductions?

740111215.text: Hmm... If what you say is true, then this was actually a book of prophecies, wasn't it?

740111216.text: But why make the format so complicated? If the author didn't want people to understand it, wouldn't it have been better to not write it at all?

740111217.text: Actually, I also heard all kinds of sounds while I was meditating... But they were just the songs of birds and flowers... I don't know anything about the prophecy you spoke of.

740111218.text: It seems we must enter that space again to understand what is going on... If we meditate together this time, we should be able to enter it.

740111219.text: Paimon's still worried... Wait! Paimon wants to come too! No way is she gonna stay here alone.

740111224.text: Once again, you focus upon meditating, and the furor surrounding you fades. The world grows silent.\nThen, you hear the tiniest of sounds, and a feeling that is wrath, or perhaps grief, wells up within your heart.

740111225.text: Your very soul feels drawn to this mysterious sound.\nAnd as you follow that sound, a whole world — utterly alien, supremely familiar — races to meet you.

740111214.text: Eh? Did someone say anything in there? And it was some kind of prophecy? That's real creepy...

740111401.text: Wha—? Where the heck did we end up?

740111402.text: This is like some kind of dreamscape! This must be the strange place you were talking about before.

740111405.text: Did the author of the book really create this place? And they hid such a big space inside it, too...

740111406.text: Hmm... Well, Paimon doesn't know how they did it, but this place looks like a ruin!

740111407.text: Also, we meditated with Canotila to get here, but we're the only two people around right now...

740111408.text: She didn't fall somewhere, did she? Oh no! Things could get bad if she winds up in danger!

740111501.text: Huh!? Where'd Canotila go? She was just here a moment ago...

740111502.text: Wait! There's something on the ground, pick it up and take a look!

740111503.text: You pick up a page from a book...

740111504.text: Is this page the same as the ones we found before? How did it end up here?

740111506.text: It's easily readable! Is it because we're in this strange space?

740111507.text: Cataclysm? Destruction? Some kinda apocalypse? What...? Even if Paimon can read the words, it still doesn't make any sense.

740111509.text: Hmm... That's true. We've definitely seen something about "calculations" before.

740111512.text: So, does this mean that this is the future the author wants us to see?

740111513.text: A world where even Sweet Flowers and Mints won't grow — ugh, that's a terrible place no matter how you slice it!

740111514.text: But if that really is the future, shouldn't the author tell everyone about it and find a solution? Why make a place like this?

740111511.text: Huh... So it's as we guessed previously.

740112114.text: No sign of Canotila or where she's gone. There's only this fellow here...

740112101.text: That said, it doesn't seem to want to attack us anymore. That's a first for a Rifthound, huh?

740112102.text: It looks like... It wants to say something to us?

740112103.text: Not that we can understand it, anyway.

740112104.text: We shouldn't get too close... just in case.

740112106.text: What's an ordinary little doggie doing here? Where'd that Rifthound go?

740112107.text: #{NICKNAME}, take a look! Is there something wrong with Paimon's eyes?

740112110.text: Is it trying to tell us to go through that passage over there?

740112111.text: Judging from its reaction, Paimon guessed right!

740112112.text: Who knows where that's gonna lead, but we weren't able to find Canotila anywhere... so maybe she did leave via that way.

740112113.text: And it looks like there's no other route we can take, so let's just try it and see what happens!

740112302.text: Or maybe... we never even left...

740112303.text: Oh? You had the same reaction as I did, Paimon.

740112304.text: Canotila! We were looking all over for you!

740112305.text: Paimon kept calling out for you, but you never responded! That place was so dangerous, but you just ran around all over the place!

740112306.text: Dangerous? The place we entered was so serene and peaceful, like a beautiful garden.

740112307.text: Huh? But all we saw was rubble!

740112308.text: That's odd. I kept looking for you two back in that previous space. But there were big trees and flowers everywhere, so I got lost...

740112309.text: Fortunately, I followed the sound of a bird, then found a golden butterfly, which brought me up on top of the garden...

740112310.text: What about the Rifthound? We saw you and a Rifthound... Oh, right! That Rifthound even turned into a dog.

740112311.text: Ugh... Now it feels like Paimon is just talking nonsense...

740112312.text: I saw a little dog too! On top of the garden, there was a cute little dog that nodded at me, and helped open the way out for me.

740112313.text: I thought you both had gone somewhere else to play... And that I didn't need to worry, so I just came back here.

740112314.text: And you? What did you discover?

740112316.text: Though Paimon doesn't think it'll answer your questions, we did find a page...

740112319.text: You open the page you found, and show it to Canotila...

740112320.text: The butterfly... It's the golden butterfly...

740112321.text: Huh? What are you talking about?

740112322.text: I can see golden butterflies flying out from the page, just like the one I saw in the space before.

740112323.text: Ugh... Never mind solving anything, we've got even more problems on our hands now! Seems like you really did see something completely different in that space!

740112324.text: Hmm. If that space is the future predicted by the author, then why did you see a garden? Just thinking about that makes Paimon's head hurt!

740112325.text: But I was very happy inside... I didn't even think about those questions! Maybe that's what the book was trying to tell me all along.

740112326.text: Even if we perceive differently, if we can communicate our feelings to one another, maybe the "essence" of things doesn't matter all that much after all.

740112327.text: Paimon wouldn't say that we had a great time in there, but if you've figured things out for yourself, good on you!

740112328.text: Still, that place is pretty sketchy, and we don't yet have any clue as to what's up with that prophecy either.

740112329.text: Speaking of the prophecy, this book makes it sound really scary, sure, but what if the things I saw were the real future? After all, such things aren't set in stone, are they?

740112330.text: And since the book mentions other ways to enter that space, we may be able to figure this book and its prophecy out if we find them.

740112331.text: And then maybe we can meet there again, in that space!

740112332.text: Uh, it might be better if we just meet in reality. Also, Canotila, don't go running around in that space anymore!

740112318.text: Right! We found this inside, though we don't know if it'll be useful, it also looks like a page from this book...

740110302.text: Hmm... So you can't understand it at all either, after all?

740110304.text: Maybe there's some kind of cipher! Take a closer look!

740110306.text: You stare at the runes on the page for some time. The runes slowly start to disintegrate and reassemble themselves, becoming new words.\nAt the same time, your surroundings seem to recede, and you arrive in a strange new place.

740110307.text: "I see. This is a world where even Sweet Flowers and Mint cannot grow. Can you see it, too?"

740110308.text: You turn around to look for the source of the voice, but are suddenly awakened. Looking back at the book, it looks just like it did originally, as though nothing happened.

740112401.text: These do look like the missing pages from the book! Let's try putting one back in, shall we?
